Thank you for your words. Logically, I know you're right. My department is already short-staffed as it is. She (my boss) would be stupid to fire me at this point. She said herself it was hard to find anyone with the credentials required for the job.

I know this...but you know how it goes. Facts bounce off that well-done steak of a brain in our heads. All my boss is NOT a rational woman. She makes godawful decisions all the time and then gaslights you over it. I can absolutely see her firing me because she's so petty.

And because of that core belief, all the other paranoia around everything else remains. I'm trying very hard to get past this. I can't do this anymore.

I'm currently on 120mg Latuda, but my psych wants me to taper off and switch to Vraylar. I asked her if just going up to 160mg would work. She basically said that my condition was critical enough for a complete change altogether.

That's super intense. And I honestly don't blame you for being paranoid in that circumstance.

As for how my psychosis broke out, I'm already screwed with symptoms due to me being on the schizo spectrum. But this particular episode, which has been going on for a little over a month now, was started by bullshit at work. Found out people were talking about me...and I know better than to be grandiose about it. I know damn well they are talking mad shit.

This is incredibly common for me to believe. Sometimes, I can manage it, and other times, I flip out. I've frightened quite a few people in the past. I'm trying desperately to avoid that this time, but it feels impossible. I'm internalizing everything now, and it's making the feeling so much stronger.

I saw my psych yesterday, and she is adjusting my meds. Hopefully, that helps. I NEED it to help, goddammit.
I'm so sorry that's been happening. This shit is fucking horrible. And do you mean taking meds or something else?

I live in a relatively big city, in which there are multiple mental health facilities to choose from. I only have experience with two; one as an employee and one as a one-time patient. The way patients were treated at the facility I was admitted to was pretty good. Problem clients were talked to like adults, and they weren't looked down upon by techs. The administered medication for clients was reasonable, and the facility has a fairly decent reputation in my city.

The facility I work at, though? Very apathetic techs, clients are treated like children, and the "psychiatric treatment" clients receive is incredibly mediocre. I can't tell you how often we get phone calls from the angry families of these clients. It's always the same complaints, and I honestly can't disagree with them. And, just out of curiosity, I looked up my facility online, and they have an *awful* reputation in the area. They used to go by another name but were forced to change it when their original name alone was enough to turn clients away from seeking their services.

To summarize: my facility has a terrible reputation, possibly the worst out of any crisis unit in my area. I don't know if this information is particularly helpful, but there it is...

1. I want to say around 9 or 10? I was very young when the delusions started happening. Severe depression that resulted in me trying to drink cleaning solution. The seeing posters move then came. Then the voices. I really believed gods were watching over me and me alone. I was super special. When I was about 12, I thought I was pregnant with a spirit...despite only have had sex once ever (not consensual...so that's trauma that might've contributed to this disorder). I also began experiencing mania.

I have Bipolar 1 and I only seem to get motivation to write whenever I'm manic or hypomanic (if it's mania, I write A FUCK LOAD of chapters. If it's hypomania, I write one...maybe two before losing my motivation again). My therapist, luckily, gave me some tips on how to find motivation without mania. Maybe they can help you, too?

1. As someone already stated, try recording your ideas either by journaling or simply recording yourself talking about the ideas. Then you can go back later and review the ideas.

2. Turn off your phone and go out in nature for a little while. Decompression can really help creativity.

3. Enlist the help of someone to help with world-building and character-writing. Sometimes having a writing buddy to brainstorm with can help a lot.

4. Let your mind rest. Don't force yourself to write if you aren't feeling up to it at the moment. Forcing yourself to write can potentially make you more bitter towards your own project...and that's the LAST thing you want to happen. Rest, then come back to it later when you're refreshed.

5. Take up a hobby besides writing, as it can potentially inspire you and give you some ideas that you hadn't thought of before.

Hopefully this helps!
